newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Settlers remove mobile homes from West Bank hill.
newsitem.headline: Settlers remove mobile homes from West Bank hill.

text.p: Jewish settlers on Sunday removed mobile homes they had planted on a West Bank hilltop in defiance of the Israeli government, witnesses said.

In return for their decision to dismantle the makeshift outpost set up on Friday, Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai met with settler leaders in the nearby settlement of Beit El to discuss their demands to expand the community.
"It was a very good meeting...I came to hear their essential needs (which) will be discussed in a serious manner," Mordechai told reporters.

Yoel Tsur, a Beit El resident whose wife and son were killed by Palestinian gunmen last month, said Mordechai had promised an answer "tomorrow or in two days" on the question of expanding the settlement.
Witnesses said settlers disconnected makeshift electricity and water lines from seven caravans they hauled onto a hill near Beit El north of Jerusalem under the cover of darkness last Friday.
The settlers lowered Israeli flags and towed the mobile homes down the hill under Israeli army guard.
"The government of Israel will not condone unilateral acts of settlement that are not approved by the government," Dore Gold, policy adviser to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, told Reuters.

Settlers called the caravan placement a "protest action" against the government's delay in allowing them to expand Beit El. They plan the expansion as a response to the killing of Tsur's wife and son.
"It's like when a woman gives birth -- you need to push a little," said Beit El settler Yaakov Katz, referring to pressure on the government to widen settlement.
Settlers feel Netanyahu has betrayed election promises to further settlement in lands they deem the biblical birthright of the Jewish people.

Since taking office in June, Netanyahu has authorised the building of some 3,000 homes in existing settlements, according to Israeli peace activist figures. He has not started any new settlements, a move Palestinians have warned would cause an explosion.
Some 130,000 Jews live in settlements scattered among more than two million Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza, areas captured by Israel in the 1967 war.
